summary: This standards-track RFC defines a new OSPF Router Information TLV that lets OSPF routers flood S-BFD Discriminator values tied to a target network identifier. It works with both OSPFv2 and OSPFv3.

eli5.summary: Routers using OSPF share S-BFD ID numbers with the whole network.

questions: how does ospf advertise s-bfd discriminators
what is ospf router information tlv type 11
does s-bfd tlv trigger spf in ospf
subtitle: How OSPF routers tell each other which S-BFD discriminators reach which targets.

tldr.problem: Seamless BFD uses 4-octet discriminators to identify network targets, so an S-BFD initiator needs a way to learn which discriminator belongs to which target.
tldr.mechanism: A new optional TLV, the S-BFD Discriminator TLV (type 11), is carried in the OSPF Router Information LSA and flooded to other routers in OSPFv2 and OSPFv3.
tldr.outcome: Every OSPF node can store the discriminators so initiators can build S-BFD probes. Routers that do not understand the TLV ignore it, so nothing breaks.

today: RFC 7884 is a Proposed Standard and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It depends on the S-BFD mechanism defined in RFC 7880.

sections.title: Why Advertise Discriminators
sections.content:
Seamless Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (S-BFD, RFC 7880) is a simplified way of using BFD with many negotiations removed. It does this by identifying network targets with 4-octet discriminators that are unique within an administrative domain.

These discriminators can be advertised by the interior gateway protocols. RFC 7884 covers OSPF: it defines a new TLV, the S-BFD Discriminator TLV, carried in the OSPF Router Information (RI) Link State Advertisement (LSA) from RFC 7770. It works for both OSPFv2 and OSPFv3.
sections.eli5: For routers to check on each other quickly, each one needs to know the others' ID numbers. This RFC is about sharing those numbers.

sections.title: How OSPF and S-BFD Relate
sections.content:
S-BFD assigns one or more discriminators to each S-BFD reflector node. OSPF learns about them from S-BFD and floods them in the new TLV. Once flooded, the information is stored in all OSPF nodes, so S-BFD initiators can map target nodes to target discriminators and construct the S-BFD probe.

When several discriminators are advertised, the RFC leaves the mapping of a given discriminator to a specific use case out of scope.
sections.eli5: A router that wants to ping a friend looks up the friend's number in a shared phone book. OSPF is the phone book that everyone gets a copy of.

sections.title: The S-BFD Discriminator TLV
sections.content:
The TLV is OPTIONAL. It has a 16-bit Type field (value 11), a 16-bit Length field, and then one or more 4-octet discriminators. Length is the total length of the discriminators in octets, so it is four times the number of discriminators, with no optional padding.

If a router has several instances of the OSPFv2 or OSPFv3 Router Information LSA, the discriminators of that router are the union of all discriminators in all advertised non-MaxAge instances. A receiving router may decide to install a discriminator in its BFD target identifier table.

Routers that do not recognize the TLV type ignore it, as RFC 7770 specifies, and so do not learn S-BFD discriminators through OSPF.
sections.eli5: The message is a small envelope: a label saying what is inside, a note saying how long it is, and then a list of ID numbers.

sections.title: Flooding Scope and Updates
sections.content:
The TLV travels in the Router Information LSA: OSPFv2 Opaque type 4 with Opaque ID 0, or OSPFv3 with function code 12. The flooding scope is chosen by the Opaque LSA type in OSPFv2 and by the S1/S2 bits in OSPFv3.

  • Area-local scope: the TLV MUST be in an OSPFv2 type 10 RI LSA, or an OSPFv3 RI LSA with S1 set and S2 clear.
  • Whole IGP domain: the TLV MUST be in an OSPFv2 type 11 RI LSA, or an OSPFv3 RI LSA with S1 clear and S2 set.

When an S-BFD reflector is deactivated, the advertising router MUST originate a new RI LSA without the corresponding TLV, provided other TLVs remain. If none remain, it MUST either send an empty RI LSA or purge it by prematurely aging it.

Inside an area, the information is only current and usable when the advertising router is itself reachable through OSPF-calculated paths in that area. For domain-wide flooding from a remote area, the mechanism in Section 5 of RFC 5250 should be used. Discriminators are expected to change very rarely, and a change MUST NOT trigger any SPF computation at a receiving router.
sections.eli5: You can choose to share the number with just your neighborhood or with the whole city. If a router stops answering, it takes its number off the list. Changing the list does not make everyone redraw their maps.

sections.title: Compatibility and Security
sections.content:
The TLV introduces no interoperability issues. A router that does not support it silently ignores it, as RFC 7770 specifies.

Security of discriminator distribution relies on the security of OSPF, since the information stays within an administrative domain. OSPF has no encryption for LSAs, so the advertisement is not private. The RFC says this is not a concern, because there is no need to hide the discriminator value that can be used to reach the reflectors.

IANA assigned TLV codepoint 11 for the S-BFD Discriminator TLV in the "OSPF Router Information (RI) TLVs" registry.
sections.eli5: Older routers just skip the new note, so nothing gets confused. The number is not a secret, so it is fine that others can read it.

fields.name: Length
fields.desc: Four times the number of discriminators.
